The Discourse on Liberation:
Is it the case that a mind possessed by lust is liberated?
Yes, it is.
Is it that a mind accompanied by lust, born together with lust, conjoined with lust, associated with lust,
co-existent with lust, following after lust— an unwholesome, worldly, cankerous, fetterable,
bondable, floodable, yokeable, hindering, misapprehended, graspable, and defiled mind— is liberated?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Consciousness is liberated together with contact; are both contact and consciousness liberated? Yes.
"A mind with lust is liberated; both lust and the mind are liberated"?
One should not say this... [and so on] ...
"A mind accompanied by feeling"... [and so on].
Is it that the mind— possessing perception,
possessing volition, and possessing wisdom— is liberated, such that both wisdom and the mind are liberated?
“Yes,” [you say].
“A mind accompanied by lust is liberated; both lust and the mind are liberated”?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is it the case that a mind accompanied by contact and accompanied by lust is liberated, and both the contact and the mind are liberated?
Yes. Are both the lust and the mind liberated?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … consciousness accompanied by feeling is with lust … [as before] … consciousness accompanied by perception is with lust … [as before].
If a conscious mind accompanied by lust …pe… a wise mind accompanied by lust is liberated, are both wisdom and the mind liberated? Yes.
“Both passion and the mind are liberated”?
One should not say so… [and so on] … “A mind accompanied by hatred is liberated”? One should not say so… [and so on].
“Yes,” you say.

But can it be said that a mind which is accompanied by hatred, born together with hatred, conjoined with hatred, associated with hatred, co-existent with hatred, following after hatred—an unwholesome, worldly, tainted mind …pe… a defiled mind—is liberated?
Certainly not; such a thing cannot be said …pe….
“The mind with contact is liberated; both contact and the mind are liberated,” is that so? Yes.
“The mind with hatred is liberated; both hatred and the mind are liberated,” is that so?
It should not be stated thus …pe… [it is] with feeling …pe… with perception …pe…
If it is admitted that the conscious mind— indeed, the mindful and wise mind— is liberated, and that both wisdom and the mind are liberated, then [is this not so]?
Yes, it is.
"A mind accompanied by hatred is liberated; both hatred and the mind are liberated"?
One should not say this... [and so on] ...
"A mind accompanied by contact and accompanied by hatred is liberated; both contact and the mind are liberated"? One should not say this... [and so on].
“Yes,” you say.
“A mind affected by hatred is liberated; both hatred and the mind are liberated”?
You should not say so… [and so on].
Feeling accompanied by hatred...
perception accompanied by hatred...
volition accompanied by hatred...
"A mind accompanied by wisdom and accompanied by hatred is liberated; both wisdom and the mind are liberated," you say?
"Yes.
"Then hatred and the mind are both liberated?"
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does a mind accompanied by delusion become liberated? Yes.

“Is it the case that a mind accompanied by delusion, born together with delusion, conjoined with delusion, associated with delusion, co-existent with delusion, following after delusion—an unwholesome, worldly, tainted, and defiled mind—is liberated?
“One should not say so.
… [as before] … “Does a mind accompanied by contact become liberated, and do both contact and the mind become liberated?”
“Yes,” [you say].
“A mind accompanied by delusion is liberated, and both delusion and the mind are liberated”?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
With feeling...
with perception...
with volition...
"The mind with wisdom is liberated; both wisdom and the mind are liberated"?—Yes.
"The mind with delusion is liberated; both delusion and the mind are liberated"?—[No].

It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Does a consciousness accompanied by contact and accompanied by delusion become liberated, such that both the contact and the consciousness are liberated? Yes.
“Both delusion and consciousness are liberated”?

Is it that a consciousness accompanied by perception and delusion... accompanied by volition and delusion...
[and so on] ...accompanied by wisdom and delusion is liberated, such that both wisdom and consciousness are liberated?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then both delusion and consciousness are liberated?
One should not speak thus… [and so on]…
Is it the case that a mind accompanied by lust, accompanied by hatred, and accompanied by delusion is liberated?
Yes. Is it the case that a mind free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion, and free from defilement is liberated? Yes.
If that cannot be said … [as before] … then it must not be said that “a mind with lust,
with hatred, and with delusion is liberated.”
The Discussion on Liberation is finished.
